content.what: Models read from the run's shared HF cache (HF_HOME preset by the platform) instead of ./hf_cache
content.why: Platform rule: never override HF_HOME/TRANSFORMERS_CACHE (avoids duplicate weights); no workspace hf_cache exists

content.what: vLLM 0.11.0 run with enforce_eager=True, max_num_seqs=48 (plan: 16), generation_config='vllm'
content.why: Container has no C compiler for Triton/Inductor; max_num_seqs only changes throughput; generation_config='vllm' guarantees the HF sampling defaults (T=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20) are never merged

content.what: Program extraction keeps only top-level imports/defs/classes/assignments for EVERY arm (plan: template-free arms only)
content.why: Identical rule across arms so module-level demo code (prints, example calls) can never crash an otherwise valid chat solution

content.what: Steering arms use a custom decode loop (Gumbel-max over full-vocab float32 logits at T=1, one CUDA generator per (task, paraphrase, sample)) instead of HF generate + torch.manual_seed per batch
content.why: Exact per-sample common-random-number coupling independent of batch composition (verified: hook test f2), and HF generation_config can never leak in; each batch holds 2 arms x 10 samples of one paraphrase (no padding) for ~2x throughput

content.what: Uniform no-code cutoff for all HF arms: a row is stopped at 512 tokens if neither ``` nor 'def solve' has appeared (finish_reason nocode_cutoff, counted as degenerate)
content.why: Sharpening arms produced pure garbage running to 1024 tokens; the rule is arm-blind, never fires on S0, and was applied post hoc (identically) to the 20 rows generated before it existed

content.what: Runtime labeller rules refined (revision rounds 1-2): IDDFS restart = >=4 waves of start-neighbour reads after reads at start-distance >=4 AND re-read ratio >=5; Bellman-Ford/SPFA from edge-list passes, edge-order sensitivity, or FIFO re-enqueues (deque and list queues) instead of exponent band [1.6,2.6)
content.why: The exponent band mislabels O(n^2) array Dijkstra as Bellman-Ford and the first wave rule fired on level-synchronous BFS; array-scan Dijkstra and Dial stay 'unknown' at runtime by design and are resolved by AST/judge

content.what: AST labeller: added level-synchronous BFS (frontier lists swapped each round) and made the Floyd-Warshall X[i][k]+X[k][j] pattern require three distinct named indices
content.why: Gate failures on a level-BFS variant and a false FW hit on pf[0][0]+pb[0][0] in bidirectional Dijkstra

content.what: Blind judge (google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite) labels every distinct parseable program, not only disagreements; the FINAL label still follows the plan rule (runtime==AST catalogue label, else judge)
content.why: Cost ~$0.0001/call; gives a full-sample judge-label sensitivity analysis and agreement rates per arm in addition to the 15-per-arm audit

content.what: Judge 'other:<sub>' labels that name a catalogue algorithm (e.g. buggy_bfs, incorrect_dijkstra_attempt) are canonicalised to that algorithm, arm-blind
content.why: The judge was instructed to label buggy programs by the algorithm they attempt but sometimes emitted other:buggy_X

content.what: PREDICT primary predictor = base_tf all parseable labelled samples restricted to survivors (fallback 3), with the correct-only version committed as first secondary
content.why: Only 12 (T1) and 18 (T2) correct base_tf samples (<40 per task); decided and hash-committed before phase C was sampled

content.what: Ban prompts use the ban sentence itself as the lead-in segment (SEG = B_i), no neutral lead-in
content.why: Literal reading of STEP 2.2-2.3 (SEG + spec); identical across base and instruct ban arms

content.what: Neutral segments P10..P49 built from 10 opener templates x 8 object phrases (P0..P9 verbatim from the plan)
